title: The Nature of the Body and the Son of Perdition
english: Regarding being subject to wrath according to condemnation, he calls them children of wrath, as Paul says: 'And we were by nature children of wrath, as the rest' (Rom 3:23). These are able to change, so as to no longer be children of wrath by nature.

Paul, indeed, concerning himself and those holy ones who were similarly made, says: 'We were by nature children of wrath, as also the rest of the men, being still here in the sinning' (Rom 3:23). But 'by nature' signifies not according to nature, but according to truth. For 'We were by nature children of wrath,' he says, declares that the sinning ones are truly accountable to wrath; just as a child of wrath is made by the indwelling of evil, so having changed, one becomes a child of truth.

For such things were said concerning some by the Savior: 'Wisdom was justified from her children,' calling the wise children of wisdom. Since being children of someone, they have being from the one who begot them; but those who have being from the quality of that which has come to them also have it; it is fitting that those who make themselves children and sons of a quality are so named.

Just as such things were said by the Savior, 'These are the wise, children of wisdom'; so also he summoned other sons of peace, asserting to the disciples: 'If you enter into a city, or into a house, and there is a son of peace, your peace, being given to the city or to the house, will rest upon the one existing in it as a son of peace' (Luke 10:6). Again the same Savior says: 'The sons of this age are more prudent than the sons of light, in their own generation' (John 12:35); calling sons of light those who have been enlightened by the knowledge of the truth and by the works of virtue. Toward whom he says, 'You are the light of the world' (John 12:36), because they are children of light; but those loving the present life, and lifting up all things toward it which they do, he named sons of this age. But even if he said these are more prudent than the sons of light, he did not say they are more prudent absolutely, but in their own generation; that is, in the things pertaining to this age, they are found more prudent than the sons of light. For they are wise for doing evil, but they have not known how to do well. And concerning Judas it has been written, that he might be a son of perdition (John 17:12). For the Lord said concerning him, 'No one is lost...'

[He calls] one of my disciples a son of perdition. And he called him a son of perdition because of what was done regarding perdition. For when he was one of the apostles and served alongside those with the Savior, he was not such a person; but when he became a traitor to the Son of God and Teacher, having loved the silver of perdition. And because he was not evil by nature, while being among all the disciples, he heard: 'Behold, I send you as sheep in the midst of wolves' (Matt 10:16). If he says that the sinners are wolves and the practitioners of virtue are sheep, if Judas had been evil by nature, he would not have been a sheep of Christ; since the one who is evil by nature is not a practitioner of virtue. But even the devil is not evil by nature, but [is so] by way of his own free will.

Just as so, not only the wicked, but also the diligent and the practiced ones are called sons and children, those who carry out [actions] in the aforementioned way, according to which it was said that those receiving from them [the qualities] are called offspring of qualities, which they possess from the quality; it is not said that anyone is flesh of sin or body of sin absolutely, but rather [that they are so] by serving sin. For the man, using the body and the flesh for lust and other such activities, makes his body a body of sin and the flesh a flesh of sin; just as the diligent one, through temperance and the following virtue, sanctifies his body and his soul. The virgin, therefore, becomes holy in body and spirit, which is the soul, as Paul writes, saying that the virgin must be unattached to worldly affairs, so that she may be holy in body and spirit (1 Cor 7:34).

But he also writes in the Epistle to the Corinthians: 'Glorify God in your body' (1 Cor 6:20). And if God is glorified in the body of men, God is not glorified in evil; the body is not evil by nature, even if the sinner makes it evil by using it sinfully. And shortly after, he calls out to the same [people] again: 'Do you not know that your bodies are a temple of the Holy Spirit in you, which you have from God?' (1 Cor 6:19). If anyone destroys the temple of God, God destroys him; for the temple of God is holy, which you are. But also in the [epistle] to the Thessalonians, the same apostle writes: 'May the God of peace sanctify you completely, and your whole [being]...' (1 Thess 5:23).
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.

title: The Likeness of Sinful Flesh
english: May your spirit, and the soul, and the body be preserved blamelessly in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ. For how can anyone have the body entirely sanctified and completely, if the body is not capable of being sanctified, it not being by nature evil? If indeed this is evil by nature, it is not receptive to sanctification; but if it receives the good, it is clear that it is not evil by nature, being receptive to the good. For that which is evil by nature is not receptive to the good, just as that which is good by nature is not receptive to evil.

The same Apostle writes to certain people in another Epistle: 'Let us cleanse ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, accomplishing holiness in the fear of God' (2 Cor 7:1), showing also by this word how the flesh is able to be cleansed of the defilements of sin that attach to it. But also the spirit and the soul; for if the flesh were evil in essence, and the spirit were good in essence, then neither would the spirit have defilement, nor would the flesh be cleansed from defilement. But he protects both the clean from defilement, saying also the manner of the cleansing. For, he says, accomplishing holiness in the fear of God. And it is well said: 'In the fear of God,' showing that they have obedience, and not out of necessity. If, accomplishing holiness in the fear of God, we cleanse our own flesh from defilement and the spirit, it is clear that this happens when sanctification approaches us; for just as the soul of ignorance and of the unrighteous is cleansed by the presence of knowledge and righteousness—for the avoidance of evil works out the entrance of virtue from the opposite—so the flesh is cleansed of defilement and the spirit by the presence of sanctification.

And in these things, 'spirit' means the soul, just as in the Acts of the Apostles, Stephen the apostle, being left behind and about to die, said while praying: 'Lord Jesus, receive my spirit' (Acts 7:59). For he was not saying anything else as his spirit in these things, except the soul. If, therefore, through many things—sometimes of sin, sometimes of sanctification, and having them for the purpose of glorifying God—the flesh and the spirit are spoken of, none of these is evil or good by nature; but they are each, by their own will, receptive; or rather, according to the use of the one possessing them, they receive, at times, to be of sin, and at times, to be of sanctification. And if, even while being ignorant of the explicit meaning, from which is brought...

They think that flesh is the sin of sin; but we, having established the whole matter, will make the reasoning clear. It is thus: God, having sent His Son in a likeness of sinful flesh, judged sin in the flesh through the sin.

What he says is such: The flesh of all men has its being from union, apart from the first-formed one whom the Savior took up. For no human body would come to be otherwise than if the male were joined to the female. Since, therefore, the Savior took a body from the Virgin alone, not having the beginning from union, He called the Lord's flesh a likeness of the flesh [that comes] from union. For He did not say at all that He has a likeness of flesh, but a likeness of sinful flesh. And the likeness of sinful flesh is flesh, lacking only in this from the other three kinds of flesh: that it has had its existence without a man. For it was necessary that he coming for the salvation of men should not take a body from union. Nor should he take it from outside the succession of men, like the first man, so that his body might not be considered heterogeneous. For if he himself had also been joined from the earth, as the leader of the human race, those introducing the opinion through fantasy would have had the suspicion that he did not bring a human body according to truth. Again, if he had taken a body from union, not having the sin passed over, he himself would have been considered responsible for that sin, through which all those from Adam exist in succession. If they were to say: 'If the flesh born from the union of man and woman is the flesh of sin, then marriage is evil'; let them hear that before the arrival of the Savior, who took away the sin of the world, all men, just as they practiced all other things with wickedness, also had marriage sinfully. Because of this, the bodies born from marriage must be understood correctly. And so, since the conjunction of Adam and Eve happened after the sin, for this reason it is called the flesh of sin. For being incorruptible before the transgression, it became corruptible through transgression; and so the succession has the corruptible. The Savior, therefore, had a likeness of this flesh, even if His flesh did not see corruption. But, as the arrival of the Savior has occurred, as a removal of sin from other things has happened, so also from...

title: Kinds of Volitional Evil
english: Regarding marriage. Now indeed those living according to the Gospel are able to have an honorable marriage and an undefiled bed, as Paul writes to the believers: 'Marriage is honorable, and the bed undefiled; but fornicators and adulterers God will judge' (Hebrews 13:4). For by distinguishing the honorable marriage and those using it from fornicators and adulterers, he does not want this to be fornication or adultery; therefore marriage is not even a sin.

And it will be said more naturally: Virginity turns out to be a divine thing, and exists in virtues. If anyone therefore, comparing marriage to this, says it is a sin, it is not a sin in an absolute sense. For the evil is not a sin by being a comparison to the good, but being such in itself. If ever indeed one were to say something evil as being toward a good, and that itself were good, it would be inferior to the good he is setting forth as prior.

Those then coming to the Gospel first come to it regarding godliness, and to become wise according to God. These therefore have the being fought against by some; for it is necessary for these to firmly take up Christianity. And firmness approaches from the training according to the trials. Therefore it is necessary for them to endure struggles.

And just as those competing, if they cared for the reasonable, do not combine this with that as it happens; not as an athlete, but with much precision, aiming at the proportion of each one's strength; so also our athlete, Christ, does not yoke together all with the same opponents. But according to the age and the strength of each, he gives the adversary.

To the Corinthians, being still infants, Paul writes that they are surrounded by the sufferings of the flesh: 'You have not suffered temptation except what is human' (1 Corinthians 10:13). For the temptations of these, and the struggles, have reference to human matters. And concerning himself and those nearby, both unstable and strong, writing he says: 'For our wrestling is not against blood and flesh, but against the rulers, and the authorities, and the cosmic powers of the darkness of this age' (Ephesians 6:12); saying this only once: 'For us who have ascended above, the wrestling is no longer against blood and flesh, that is, human things, but against the ranks having ascended above the adversaries'; and these are kinds of...

of the logical [kinds], having become evil by choice. But let no one suppose that, because we have spoken of kinds of logical evils, we are speaking of an evil essence. For there are kinds and genera of those things which are volitional.

For we say, for example, that there are kinds of being excellent, just, temperate, and wise. Since virtue is a genus, being divided into kinds, into justice, temperance, and the rest, it is necessary that one participating in the genus be called excellent, just as a genus is that of those participating in virtues according to kind; likewise, since science is a genus, of grammar, music, and the rest, we say that the one called a scientist from the genus is a genus of those called from the kinds of science.

So if then we speak of kinds of logical evils, we say that all those under these kinds are such by choice. Therefore, let it be manifest that the aforementioned names are not of essences, but of volitional [matters]. For the name 'devil' denotes not an essence, but a choice.

Immediately also, regarding Judas, a man, the Lord named him 'devil,' not because of his essence, but because of his choice, saying to all the disciples at once, counting Judas among them: 'Did I not choose you, the twelve, and one of you is a devil?' (John 6:70). As the writer brings it forth: He said this concerning Judas, the one about to betray him. For if he was called a devil because of the coming betrayal, he was not a devil then, when he also shared the election with all. For he had become elect among all, because of the virtue present in him then; but he was called a devil when he performed the things of the betrayal.

If, therefore, the name 'devil' in the case of Judas is a sign of a volitional act, so if the voice were speaking concerning anyone else, it would signify something volitional. And custom also knows the use of this name. We call 'devils' those who accuse this one of that, and those, of these. Since also the devil accuses God to men, and men to God, and those men to one another, he has received this name. And if even the name 'Satan' were accusing this same devil, let them know that even this too is a sign of some volitional [matter]. For being a Hebrew word, it is not something else...
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
